md_description: This workflow represents acute rodent brain slice electrophysiology with pharmacological manipulation and patch-clamp recording to study neurotransmitter receptor effects on synaptic plasticity. It produces raw electrophysiology traces, derived synaptic response metrics, and a metadata table summarizing the experimental setup, causal interactions, and literature support.

rodent_brain_slice.reasoning: For the rodent_brain_slice Entity node, I included only intrinsic specimen attributes that define what the slice is: species, strain, age, sex, brain region, and slice viability/state. I excluded preparation protocol details, pharmacology, recording settings, raw file properties, and derived metrics because those belong to downstream Process, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. I also avoided experiment-wide identifiers and any fields likely to overlap with already_generated metadata elsewhere in the DAG, keeping this node focused on the sample identity and origin needed to interpret later electrophysiology steps.

md_schema.descr: Rodent species from which the brain slice was obtained, recorded at the entity level before any slicing or electrophysiology. Use standard taxon names such as mouse (Mus musculus) or rat (Rattus norvegicus).
Rodent strain or line of the source animal, captured as an intrinsic origin attribute of the slice before preparation. Example: C57BL/6J, Sprague-Dawley.
Age of the source rodent in postnatal days at the time the brain slice was prepared. Record the animal age, not the slice age. Typical range for acute slice electrophysiology is roughly P7–P120.
Biological sex of the source rodent, recorded for the donor animal before tissue collection. Allowed values are exhaustive for this schema.

Anatomical brain region from which the acute slice was prepared, as the intrinsic tissue origin for the electrophysiology experiment. Example values include hippocampus, cortex, cerebellum, striatum, amygdala.
Type of acute tissue slice used as the source material for patch-clamp recording, captured as an intrinsic preparation class. Typical values may distinguish coronal, sagittal, or horizontal slices.
Thickness of the brain slice at the time it was prepared, in micrometers. Record the nominal slice thickness after sectioning; typical acute slice ranges are about 150–500 micrometer.

Qualitative condition of the slice as an entity-level descriptor of whether the tissue was suitable for downstream patch-clamp recording. This captures intrinsic preparation status, not a protocol parameter or recording quality flag.

slice_preparation.reasoning: I corrected the slice_preparation schema by removing the colliding field slice_thickness_micrometer, which had already been generated for an upstream DAG step. I retained only process-level preparation variables that describe how the slice was handled and maintained, while excluding specimen identity, recording configuration, raw data properties, and downstream analytical outputs. The remaining fields are focused on reproducibility of the acute preparation stage without duplicating earlier metadata.

md_schema.descr: Name of the dissection solution used during tissue removal and initial handling of the brain before slicing. Record the exact solution name used in this experiment, for example sucrose-based ACSF or chilled cutting solution.

Temperature of the dissection solution or tissue handling environment during brain extraction and slicing, in degrees Celsius. Record the temperature at the time of preparation; typical acute-slice values are about 0–8 Celsius for chilled dissection or 20–34 Celsius for warmer protocols.
Method or instrument used to cut the acute brain slice during preparation. Example values: vibratome, microslicer, tissue chopper.

Temperature used for post-cut recovery incubation of the acute slice, in degrees Celsius. Measure and record this during the recovery stage after slicing and before recording; common values are approximately 22–37 Celsius depending on protocol.
Duration of the post-cut recovery incubation for the acute slice, in minutes. Record the time spent in recovery medium before patch-clamp recording; typical values are about 15–120 minutes.
Name of the physiological holding or recovery solution used to maintain the slice after cutting and before recording. Example: standard ACSF, oxygenated ACSF, protective recovery solution.
Gas mixture used to oxygenate and maintain the slice during preparation and recovery, typically applied to the holding solution. Record the exact mixture used, such as 95% O2 / 5% CO2.

Method used to control pH and temperature conditions during slice recovery and maintenance. Describe the preparation-level control strategy, such as continuous carbogen bubbling or temperature-regulated incubation.

Total time from slice cutting to the end of the preparation recovery period, in minutes. Record this as a protocol timing field to support reproducibility of acute slice viability and readiness for recording.

pharmacological_modulation.reasoning: For the pharmacological_modulation Process node, I included only intervention parameters that describe how drugs were applied to the prepared slice. I excluded specimen identity, slice preparation details, patch-clamp instrument settings, raw signal properties, and derived metrics because those belong to other node types. I also avoided repeating any previously generated field names or equivalent content, and I did not reuse slice thickness after the collision was flagged. The fields focus on reproducibility of the drug manipulation: agent identity, target system, concentration, exposure timing, delivery mode, and washout.

md_schema.descr: Name of the pharmacological agent applied to the prepared slice to modulate neurotransmitter release or receptor activity. Record the exact compound used in this step, for example CNQX, APV, bicuculline, baclofen, or naloxone.

Neurotransmitter system or receptor class targeted by the applied pharmacological agent at the time of modulation. Record the intended biological target rather than the measured outcome; examples include glutamatergic, GABAergic, cholinergic, dopaminergic, or serotonergic systems.

Final concentration of the pharmacological agent in the bath or application medium, in micromolar. Record the concentration experienced by the slice during modulation; typical values span approximately 0.001–1000 micromolar depending on compound potency.
How the pharmacological agent was delivered to the prepared slice during modulation. Use one of the controlled delivery modes below, such as bath application or local puff application.

Duration of exposure of the slice to the pharmacological agent, in minutes. Measure from the start of effective application to the end of exposure; typical acute slice exposures range from seconds to tens of minutes.
Whether the pharmacological agent was washed out after application and before or during subsequent recording/analysis. Record true if a washout period was explicitly used, otherwise false.

Duration of the post-application washout period, in minutes, if washout was performed. Leave unreported only if the experiment did not include washout; typical washout durations are about 5–60 minutes.

Expected pharmacological action on the target receptor or neurotransmitter signaling pathway as intended in this process step. Use this to indicate whether the compound was used to inhibit, activate, potentiate, or block signaling.

patched_slice.reasoning: For the patched_slice Entity node, I included only intrinsic state of the prepared slice after pharmacological treatment and before capture: whether it is alive/usable, how long it has been under treatment, and whether it was stabilized in a recording chamber or perfusion setup. I excluded drug identity, concentration, and exposure protocol because those belong to the upstream pharmacological_modulation Process, and I excluded recording hardware/settings because those belong to the downstream Capture node. I also avoided repeating slice identity fields already generated for the rodent_brain_slice entity.

md_schema.descr: Condition of the acute slice after pharmacological treatment and immediately before patch-clamp measurement, recorded as an entity-level usability assessment. This is a specimen state, not a drug protocol or a recording quality flag.

Time in minutes between the start of pharmacological exposure and the point at which the slice was positioned for synaptic response measurement. Record this as a specimen-state timing attribute, not as the application duration itself.

Whether the pharmacologically treated slice had been transferred into the recording chamber or remained in a holding environment at the time this entity was defined. This captures preparation state, not instrument configuration.

Orientation of the prepared slice when positioned for synaptic response measurement, if relevant to the experiment. Example values may indicate whether the cut surface or target region faced the perfusion flow or electrode access path.

Qualitative assessment of how accessible the recorded region was to the patch pipette after pharmacological treatment, captured as an entity-level property of the prepared slice. Use this to describe whether target cells were easy, moderate, or difficult to access.

patch_clamp_recording.reasoning: For the patch_clamp_recording Capture node, I included only instrument configuration and session settings that define how the electrophysiological measurement was performed. I excluded specimen properties from the slice entities, drug manipulation details from the pharmacological process, raw file properties from the Signal node, and derived synaptic metrics from later steps. In line with the DAG guidance, I also included active hardware description fields such as amplifier and digitizer information, since those belong on the Capture node. The resulting fields capture the measurement session, electrode/pipette setup, and acquisition parameters needed to reproduce the recording conditions.

md_schema.descr: Whole-cell patch-clamp configuration used for the recording session, describing the active electrophysiological access mode established on the prepared slice. Record the configuration used at the time of acquisition, such as voltage-clamp or current-clamp.
Manufacturer of the electrophysiology amplifier used during the patch-clamp recording session. Record the instrument brand that actively acquired the synaptic response signals.
Model name or number of the electrophysiology amplifier used for patch-clamp acquisition. Example format: MultiClamp 700B, Axopatch 200B.
Serial number of the patch-clamp amplifier used for the recording session, if available. Use the manufacturer-assigned serial identifier for instrument traceability.
Model of the headstage used with the amplifier during patch-clamp recording. Record the active hardware interface that connects the electrode to the amplifier.
Model of the analog-to-digital converter or acquisition digitizer used to sample the electrophysiology signal during recording. Example: Digidata 1550B.

Digitization sampling rate used during the patch-clamp acquisition session, in hertz. Record the actively configured rate at which the raw current or voltage trace was sampled; typical values are about 5,000–100,000 Hz or higher depending on protocol.

Analog or digital low-pass filter cutoff applied during patch-clamp acquisition, in kilohertz. Record the configured bandwidth limit used at the time of measurement; typical values are about 1–10 kHz for whole-cell recordings.

Series resistance measured during the recording session, in megaohms. Record this quality-control value at the time of whole-cell break-in and during stable acquisition; typical values are approximately 5–30 megaohms.

Percent series/access resistance compensation configured on the amplifier during recording, if used. Record the active compensation setting at acquisition time; typical values are 0–100 percent depending on the protocol.

Bath or chamber temperature maintained during the patch-clamp recording session, in degrees Celsius. Record the actively controlled measurement temperature at acquisition time; typical values are approximately 20–37 Celsius.

Membrane holding potential applied during the patch-clamp recording session, in millivolts. Record the command potential used while acquiring synaptic responses; typical values are about -80 to +40 millivolt depending on clamp mode.

Maximum acceptable series resistance for retaining a recording in the acquisition session, in megaohms. Record the QC threshold applied during or immediately after acquisition to determine whether the cell was kept for analysis.

raw_ephys_traces.reasoning: For the raw_ephys_traces Signal node, I included only raw data artefact properties: file format, storage location, size, dimensionality, channel/time indexing, and technical recording quality flags. I excluded patch-clamp acquisition settings because those belong to the Capture node, and I excluded any processed features or biological interpretation because those belong downstream in the Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating fields already generated for the recording session while keeping the schema sufficient for locating, loading, and validating the raw trace files.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw electrophysiology trace file as stored in the dataset or acquisition archive. Use the exact filename assigned at export or acquisition, for example sample001.abf or recording_12.mtx.
File format of the raw patch-clamp trace artefact, recorded as a technical property of the signal output. Example values include ABF, DAT, CSV, HDF5, or TDMS.

Size of the raw electrophysiology file in bytes, measured for the stored artefact. Record the exact file size at the time of metadata capture; typical raw trace files range from kilobytes to gigabytes depending on duration and channel count.

Total duration of the raw trace file in seconds, measured from the start to the end of the stored electrophysiology acquisition. This is a property of the recorded signal artefact, not the acquisition session configuration.
Number of sampled time points in the raw electrophysiology trace. Use this to describe the temporal length of the stored signal; the value is determined by file duration and sampling rate.
Number of recorded channels contained in the raw trace file. Record the total active acquisition channels stored in the artefact, such as one or more voltage/current traces.

Human-readable description of the raw data dimensions and organization, such as 1D time series, multi-sweep matrix, or multi-channel time series. This describes how the signal is structured on disk rather than the scientific content.
File system or repository path where the raw electrophysiology trace is stored. Provide the exact access location used in the dataset or archive, for example a relative path or URI.
MD5 checksum of the raw trace file, used to verify artefact integrity after transfer or storage. Record the checksum string corresponding to the exact file version represented by this metadata entry.

Technical quality assessment of the raw trace as stored, indicating whether the file is usable, corrupted, incomplete, or requires inspection. This is a signal-level quality flag, not a biological interpretation.

synaptic_feature_extraction.reasoning: For the synaptic_feature_extraction Process node, I included only analysis workflow parameters that describe how features were computed from the raw traces. I excluded raw signal properties, patch-clamp acquisition settings, and the resulting feature values themselves because those belong to the Signal and Derivative nodes. I also avoided any fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG. The fields focus on the software environment, filtering, event-detection logic, and feature calculation settings needed to reproduce the extraction step.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or analysis package used to extract synaptic features from raw electrophysiology traces. Record the exact tool used at the time of processing, for example Python, SciPy, Clampfit, Neo, or a custom pipeline.
Version of the software or analysis package used for synaptic feature extraction. Record the exact version string used during processing, such as 1.10.0 or 2024.2.

Repository URL, package source, or code location for the feature extraction workflow used on the raw traces. Provide the exact source reference used to reproduce the analysis, such as a GitHub URL or package repository link.

Method used to correct baseline drift or offset prior to feature extraction from the raw trace. Record the algorithm or operational approach applied to the signal before measurement of amplitudes or latencies.

Threshold used to detect synaptic events, expressed as a multiple of the baseline standard deviation. Record the active threshold setting used during extraction; typical values are about 2–6 SD depending on the event type.

Width of the smoothing window applied to raw traces before or during feature extraction, in milliseconds. Record the actual window size used by the analysis workflow; typical values are about 0.1–10 ms.

Criteria used to exclude traces, sweeps, or segments with movement, noise, or stimulation artefacts before feature extraction. Describe the applied rule or threshold at the process level, not the resulting exclusion outcome.

Named feature set or analysis preset used to compute synaptic response metrics from the raw traces. Example values may refer to a standard amplitude-latency-plasticity feature bundle or a custom analysis preset.

Minimum event separation enforced during synaptic event detection, in milliseconds. Record the process parameter used to avoid counting overlapping events; typical values depend on stimulation protocol and noise level.

Time window after stimulation or trigger used for feature extraction, in milliseconds. Record the exact analysis window used to quantify synaptic responses; typical values are about 1–500 ms depending on the assay.

synaptic_response_metrics.reasoning: For the synaptic_response_metrics Derivative node, I included only computed result fields: the actual extracted amplitudes, latencies, plasticity indices, summary statistics, and output dimensions/quality descriptors of the derived table. I excluded raw trace properties and analysis workflow settings because those belong to the Signal and upstream Process nodes. I also avoided duplicating any previously generated fields and kept the schema focused on what a downstream user needs to interpret the computed synaptic summaries.

md_schema.descr: Computed synaptic response amplitude from the raw patch-clamp traces, reported in picoamperes. Record the derived value at the feature-extraction stage, typically measured for evoked or spontaneous events depending on the assay.

Derived latency between the stimulus or trigger and the onset or peak of the synaptic response, reported in milliseconds. Record the extracted value from the processed trace; typical values depend on the stimulation paradigm and can range from sub-millisecond to hundreds of milliseconds.
Computed rise time of the synaptic response, in milliseconds, as obtained from the processed trace. This is a derivative feature describing the shape of the response waveform.

Computed decay time constant of the synaptic response, in milliseconds, estimated from the processed trace or fitted waveform model. Record the fitted or measured value produced by the analysis workflow.

Derived paired-pulse ratio calculated from two sequential synaptic responses. Record the numeric ratio used as a plasticity-related summary metric, typically computed as response2 divided by response1.

Computed index summarizing change in synaptic strength or plasticity over time or across conditions. Record the exact scalar output produced by the analysis, such as facilitation, depression, or normalized change metric.

Derived response value normalized to its baseline or pre-stimulation level, reported as a unitless ratio or percent depending on the analysis convention. Record the processed summary statistic used for comparison across conditions.
Number of synaptic responses detected and retained in the derived metric table. This is a summary property of the computed output, not of the raw signal file.

Method used to summarize repeated synaptic measurements into a single derived value, such as mean, median, or fit-derived estimate. Record the statistic applied to generate the reported derivative outputs.

Quality assessment of the computed synaptic metrics, indicating whether the derived outputs are robust, partial, noisy, or unusable. This flag applies to the derivative result rather than the raw trace.

causal_interaction_synthesis.reasoning: For the causal_interaction_synthesis Process node, I included only interpretation and synthesis parameters that describe how derived metrics were combined into a causal summary. I excluded raw data properties, acquisition settings, and the final metadata-table content itself because those belong to the Signal, Capture, and downstream Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating any already generated fields and kept the schema focused on the analytical framing: which receptor/ligand relationships were evaluated, what comparison logic was used, what direction of effect was inferred, and what evidence criteria supported the causal claim.

md_schema.descr: High-level method used to combine derived synaptic metrics into a causal interpretation of neurotransmitter receptor effects on plasticity. Record the synthesis approach used in this step, such as comparative analysis, dose-response interpretation, perturbation-response mapping, or rule-based evidence aggregation.

Type of comparison used to infer causal impact during synthesis. Record how the manipulated condition was contrasted with its reference condition, for example drug versus control, agonist versus antagonist, or pre/post exposure.

Name of the neurotransmitter receptor or signaling pathway interpreted in the causal synthesis step. Record the specific target under evaluation, such as NMDA receptor, AMPA receptor, GABA_A receptor, or dopamine receptor subtype.

Direction of the inferred causal effect on synaptic plasticity or synaptic response metrics. Use this field to indicate whether the manipulation increased, decreased, or did not change the measured effect relative to the comparison condition.

Qualitative strength class assigned to the inferred causal effect during synthesis. This is a human-readable summary of how strong the evidence appeared after combining the derived metrics and comparison logic.

Level of evidence supporting the causal interpretation in this synthesis step, based on consistency of derived metrics, comparison design, and reproducibility. Use this as an internal confidence descriptor for the inferred interaction.

Method used, if any, to account for confounders during causal synthesis, such as normalization, stratification, or covariate adjustment. Record the analysis strategy applied before summarizing the causal effect.

Description of the baseline or reference state used to interpret the causal effect of receptor perturbation on plasticity. This should specify the comparator context, not the experimental protocol itself.
Named rule set or decision framework used to convert derived synaptic metrics into a causal interaction summary. Record the exact synthesis rubric or policy applied by the analysis workflow.
Whether published literature evidence was required before a causal interaction was accepted into the synthesis output. Record true if literature support was mandatory for inclusion, otherwise false.

neurotransmitter_plasticity_metadata.reasoning: For the neurotransmitter_plasticity_metadata Derivative node, I included only fields that belong in the final structured metadata table: the investigated neurotransmitter systems, summarized causal receptor interactions, concise experiment-context descriptors, and literature support references. I excluded upstream specimen preparation, drug application, recording settings, raw trace properties, and analysis workflow parameters because those belong to earlier Entity, Process, Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating already generated fields and focused on table-level outputs needed by downstream users to query, filter, and cite the final dataset summary.

md_schema.descr: List of neurotransmitter systems investigated in the study, as represented in the final metadata table. Include the systems actually assessed in this workflow, such as glutamatergic, GABAergic, or cholinergic systems, using a machine-readable list or semicolon-separated text if stored as a single field.

Concise summary of the causal receptor interactions identified in the study and recorded in the final metadata table. Describe the direction and nature of the interaction, for example NMDA receptor blockade decreases synaptic plasticity or GABA_A receptor modulation increases inhibitory response.

Species name reported in the final metadata table for the experimental organism used in the electrophysiology study. Use the organism designation appropriate for the dataset row, for example mouse or rat.
Brain region reported in the final metadata table for the recorded slice preparation. Use the anatomical region name as summarized for the study, such as hippocampus, cortex, or striatum.

Brief textual summary of the experimental setup captured in the final metadata table, including acute slice preparation, pharmacological modulation, and whole-cell patch-clamp recording context. This is a synthesis-level description rather than a protocol field.

Bibliographic reference to a published study that supports the reported finding or causal interaction in the final metadata table. Provide a citation string in a standard format, such as author-year-journal or DOI-based reference.
Digital Object Identifier for a supporting publication cited in the metadata table, if available. Record the DOI string exactly as published, for example 10.1038/xxxxxx.
PubMed identifier for a supporting publication cited in the metadata table, if available. Record the numeric PMID string for precise literature lookup.

Flag indicating whether the final metadata table entry is aligned with one or more supporting publications. Use this to summarize literature support status at the table level, not at the analysis-process level.

Unique identifier for the final metadata table row or record representing this experimental summary. Use a stable string identifier suitable for linking the table entry to other dataset components, for example row_001 or sample_A12_summary.
